language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<warning>The page image is turned 90°, so the Mongolian text lines run across the image instead of down it. The woodblock ink is pale. I could not read the Uighur-Mongol script reliably letter by letter at this orientation and resolution, so the main text is not transcribed rather than guessed. The Chinese margin label is legible and is transcribed below.</warning>
<scan-quality>fair</scan-quality>

<header>秘密經第五卷上一百五十</header>
<meta>The folio label in the right margin reads 秘密經第五卷上一百五十 (Secret Tantra section, volume 5, recto, folio 150). The left margin has a short Mongolian folio label, probably the folio number written out in words (likely ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ, "one hundred fifty"); this reading is uncertain. A red archival sequence number, 299, is printed outside the frame at the upper left.</meta>

<summary>This is folio 150 (recto) of volume 5 of the Secret Tantra section of a Mongolian Kanjur woodblock print, probably the Beijing edition. Only the Chinese folio label could be read. The roughly 25 lines of Mongolian text were not transcribed and remain untranslated.</summary>
